opportunities.title: Green Climate Fund funding proposals through the CGIAR System Organization (GCF-accredited entity)
opportunities.program: GCF funded activities (funding proposals; Simplified Approval Process / Project Preparation Facility as applicable) via accredited entity 'CGIAR System Organization'
opportunities.deadline_text: No call deadline; GCF funding proposals are submitted by accredited entities on a continuous basis. Accreditation term on the AE page: 'Renewal date | 29 Sep 2027'; 'Re-accreditation submission deadline (29 Mar 2027)'.
opportunities.funding_text: Accreditation scope listed by GCF: 'Size | Small'; 'ESS Category | Category C, Intermediation 3'; 'Fiduciary standards | Basic, Project management, Grant award'. No per-project amount stated on the page (check GCF 'Small' size thresholds in the accreditation framework).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Only GCF accredited entities submit funding proposals. CGIAR System Organization is accredited ('Status | Accredited'); CGIAR centers would develop/execute projects under it.
opportunities.eligible_countries: GCF-eligible developing countries; NDA no-objection letter required (standard GCF rule, not restated on the AE page).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: VERIFIED: 'CGIAR System Organization (CGIAR)' is on the official GCF Accredited Entities directory: accredited 19/20 Oct 2018, AMA executed 21 Sep 2022, effective 30 Sep 2022, renewal 29 Sep 2027. It already has one approved project, FP304 'Enhancing Sustainable Land Management and Climate-Resilient Agri-food Systems in Cote d'Ivoire (LARACI)' (approved funding proposal document dated 23 Jul 2026, status 'Under implementation'). No individual CGIAR center (CIAT, Bioversity, CIFOR-ICRAF, IWMI, IFPRI, etc.) appears separately on the GCF list, and none is an Adaptation Fund implementing entity or GEF Agency. Realistic route for the Alliance: co-develop a concept with an NDA and submit through the CGIAR System Organization, or act as executing/technical partner of another AE (FAO, IFAD, UNDP, WFP, CAF, CABEI, IDB, national DAEs). Constraint: CGIAR accreditation covers only Small-size, minimal-risk (Category C) grant projects.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Accredited entity (CGIAR System Organization) as lead; NDA no-objection; project must fit the AE's accreditation scope (Small, Category C, grant award).
opportunities.consortium_details: Accredited entity + NDA (country ownership) + executing entities (CGIAR centers, national institutions).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Climate adaptation and mitigation projects in GCF result areas (e.g., health, food and water security; livelihoods; ecosystems; forests and land use).
opportunities.required_documents: Standard GCF concept note / funding proposal package (not restated on the AE page).
opportunities.application_procedure: Engage the CGIAR System Organization's GCF focal point and the target country's NDA; submit concept note via the GCF Partner Portal through the AE; optionally request Project Preparation Facility support.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate-resilient agri-food systems and land management (cf. FP304) use climate risk analytics, EO monitoring and crop modelling directly; methods are components rather than the main output.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Only verified direct route from CGIAR to GCF; large-scale, country-owned adaptation programmes in LAC/Africa/Asia fit the Alliance mission.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance can deliver climate-information/EO/advisory components, but GCF project development takes 1-3 years, needs NDA buy-in and CGIAR System-level coordination; accreditation renewal due Sep 2027.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue as a medium-term pipeline: pick an NDA (e.g., Colombia, Honduras, Central America Dry Corridor) and co-develop a Small, low-risk climate-services/agri-adaptation concept with the CGIAR System Organization. Confirm its re-accreditation plans (submission deadline 29 Mar 2027).
opportunities.potential_partners: CGIAR System Organization (AE); NDAs; national meteorological services; FAO/IFAD/WFP as alternative AEs; CIFOR-ICRAF (FP304 experience).
opportunities.next_action: Contact the CGIAR System Organization GCF focal point about the internal pipeline process and FP304 lessons; shortlist 1-2 countries with NDAs open to a CGIAR-led concept.

opportunities.title: GCF Readiness and Preparatory Support (Country Support Modality) - delivery via NDA-nominated or accredited entity
opportunities.deadline_text: Submissions may be made at any time during the current Readiness Strategy 2024-2027 period, with a recommended proposal submission date of no later than 31 March 2027 to allow sufficient time for approval of the proposal and signing of the Readiness Financing Agreement before the end of the current Readiness Strategy 2024-2027 period on 31 December 2027.
opportunities.funding_text: Main country envelope of up to USD 4 million over four years; NAP formulation (NAP.1) up to USD 3 million; additional up to USD 3 million for NAP implementation (NAP.2) under conditions; up to USD 320,000 over four years for LDCs/SIDS liaison officers. Envelopes are per country, not per delivery partner.
opportunities.duration: Within the Readiness Strategy period ending 31 December 2027
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Requests are submitted by NDAs/focal points. 'Option 1 Direct access by a country through the NDA or other competent government ministry or agency; Option 2 Access by a country through an entity nominated by the NDA, which can be: (i) a national entity; (ii) an entity that has entered into a Readiness Framework Agreement with the GCF; or (iii) a GCF accredited entity; Option 3 Access ... through a competitive tender process involving GCF pre-qualified delivery partner'.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT/Bioversity are not GCF accredited and were not confirmed as Readiness Framework Agreement holders or pre-qualified delivery partners. Routes: (a) the NDA nominates the CGIAR System Organization (a GCF AE) as delivery partner with the Alliance executing; (b) the Alliance as subcontracted technical partner to the NDA or another delivery partner (e.g., FAO, UNDP) for climate information, NAP agri-sector risk analysis or EO/data systems; (c) GCF pre-qualified delivery partner tenders.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: NDA must request; delivery partner must be a national entity, Readiness Framework Agreement holder, GCF AE, or pre-qualified delivery partner.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Capacity building and technical assistance for country programming, direct access, NAP formulation/implementation (relevant: agricultural climate risk assessment, climate information systems, data for adaptation planning).
opportunities.required_documents: Readiness proposal via the GCF Partner Portal (templates per the guide).
opportunities.application_procedure: The NDA submits the readiness request through the GCF Partner Portal, naming its delivery partner.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate data, crop-climate risk analysis and EO for NAPs are relevant, but readiness funds capacity building rather than research.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Builds NDA relationships that feed GCF pipelines (incl. CGIAR-AE projects); time-limited (Mar 2027).
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Feasible as technical partner; depends on NDA demand and unused country envelope.
opportunities.recommendation: Explore in 1-2 countries with strong Alliance government ties (e.g., Colombia, Honduras, Kenya, Viet Nam) to propose NAP agri-sector climate risk / climate services readiness before 31 Mar 2027.
opportunities.potential_partners: NDAs, CGIAR System Organization, FAO, UNDP.
opportunities.next_action: Ask target NDAs about remaining readiness envelope and NAP.1/NAP.2 status; check whether the CGIAR System Organization would act as nominated delivery partner.

opportunities.title: Adaptation Fund project/programme proposals (regular, Large Innovation, Locally Led Adaptation windows) via accredited implementing entities - rolling submission
opportunities.program: Adaptation Fund funding windows (regular projects, innovation grants, LLA) - rolling basis
opportunities.deadline_text: 'Submissions for all funding windows are now accepted on a rolling basis (Decision B.40/59).' / 'The Adaptation Fund Board accepts and considers regular project and programme proposals on a rolling basis.'
opportunities.funding_text: Large innovation grants: 'grants of up to US$ 5 million to NIEs, RIEs and MIEs' (AF large innovation material from the 2021 round). Country caps and FY2027 set-asides not verified.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: 'Eligible parties seeking financial resources from the Adaptation Fund must submit their project and programme proposals directly through accredited National, Regional, or Multilateral Implementing Entities.'
opportunities.eligible_countries: AF-eligible developing countries (endorsement by the country's AF Designated Authority).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: VERIFIED: no CGIAR center is an AF implementing entity. The 14 MIEs are ADB, World Bank, IDB, IFAD, UNDP, UNEP, WFP, UNESCO, EBRD, UN-Habitat, WMO, UNIDO, FAO, WHO; the 9 RIEs are BOAD, OSS, SPREP, CAF, CABEI, CDB, SPC, ICIMOD, CCCCC. The Alliance can take part only as executing entity/technical partner under an IE (e.g., FAO, IFAD, WFP, CAF, CABEI, or an accredited NIE).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Accredited NIE/RIE/MIE; endorsement letter from the country's AF Designated Authority.
opportunities.consortium_details: Implementing entity + Designated Authority endorsement + executing entities.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Concrete adaptation projects; innovation (accelerators, scaling adaptation innovations); locally led adaptation.
opportunities.required_documents: AF project/programme proposal templates (Project Proposal Materials page).
opportunities.application_procedure: The IE e-mails the proposal to submissions@adaptation-fund.org (rolling); reviewed by the AFB secretariat and PPRC.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Agricultural adaptation, early warning/climate services and innovation windows can embed EO, crop modelling and advisory tools, but AF funds implementation, not research.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Strong LAC IE options (CAF, CABEI, IDB, FAO, WFP, IFAD) match the Alliance's LAC presence.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Feasible as executing partner; depends on IE pipeline and DA endorsement.
opportunities.recommendation: Approach FAO, WFP, IFAD or CABEI/CAF country teams with a climate-services/digital advisory component for upcoming AF proposals (including Large Innovation grants up to US$5m). Do not plan as lead.
opportunities.potential_partners: FAO, WFP, IFAD, CAF, CABEI, WMO, national NIEs.
opportunities.next_action: Review the AF 'Proposals Under Review' / 'Active Pipeline' pages for LAC countries and contact IEs with agri-climate projects in preparation.

opportunities.title: WFP Innovation Accelerator - rolling open applications (up to US$100,000 equity-free)
opportunities.deadline_text: 'we accept rolling applications for innovations that are working to end hunger, improve humanitarian response and build resilient food systems. We process and review applications periodically throughout the year.'
opportunities.funding_text: 'Access to up to US$100,000 equity-free funding to test the venture's scalability potential.'
opportunities.eligible_applicants: 'Your organization must be an established legal entity. It can be for profit or not-for-profit.' 'Your innovation must at least be at the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) stage. Proof-of-concept and initial traction is preferred.'
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: The legal-entity, for-profit or not-for-profit wording does not exclude international research organizations, but the programme targets ventures; an Alliance digital tool at MVP stage (e.g., climate-informed agro-advisory or yield/drought forecasting for anticipatory action) could apply directly or via a national/startup partner. Confirm with WFP first.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Testing/scaling innovations for hunger, humanitarian response and resilient food systems (sprint programme).
opportunities.required_documents: Online application form (details not shown on page).
opportunities.application_procedure: Apply via the innovation.wfp.org Apply page; applications are also considered for future topic-specific cohorts.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Digital/AI advisory and forecasting tools fit, but the programme favours operational products over research.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: WFP is a key operational partner for scaling climate services and anticipatory action; small amount.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires an MVP with traction and a product/venture framing.
opportunities.recommendation: Apply only if the team has an MVP-stage digital tool and a WFP country-office champion; otherwise monitor topic-specific cohorts (e.g., next AFCIA cohort).
opportunities.potential_partners: WFP country offices (Colombia, Honduras, Guatemala), national startups.
opportunities.next_action: Email the WFP Innovation Accelerator to confirm whether international research organizations are eligible before applying.

opportunities.title: GEF-9 (2026-2030) projects and Integrated Programs via GEF Agencies (CGIAR as executing/knowledge partner)
opportunities.program: GEF-9 Trust Fund programming (Food Systems, Forest Biomes and other Integrated Programs; focal area projects)
opportunities.deadline_text: No open call; projects are developed by GEF Agencies with countries during the cycle ('the Global Environment Facility's ninth replenishment cycle (2026-2030)').
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Only the 18 GEF Agencies (ADB, AfDB, EBRD, FAO, IDB, IFAD, UNDP, UNEP, UNIDO, World Bank Group, CI, CAF, DBSA, FECO, FUNBIO, IUCN, BOAD, WWF-US) submit projects, with country Operational Focal Point endorsement.
opportunities.eligible_countries: GEF-eligible recipient countries; Integrated Programs select countries by criteria.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: VERIFIED: no CGIAR center is a GEF Agency. The GEF-9 Programming Directions list 'Research Centers: Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR), Center for International Forestry Research and World Agroforestry (CIFOR-ICRAF)' among partners (Forest Biomes IP section). Route: executing partner or knowledge-platform/EO monitoring partner in an agency-led child project or IP global platform (FAO, IFAD, UNDP, CI, WWF, IUCN, CAF, IDB).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: GEF Agency as lead; OFP endorsement.
opportunities.cofunding_details: GEF projects require co-financing (GEF-9 ratio not verified).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Integrated Programs incl. Food Systems and Forest Biomes; the programming document cites monitoring systems ('digital platforms, remote sensing, blockchain traceability').
opportunities.application_procedure: Engage GEF Agencies' regional teams during GEF-9 PIF development and IP child-project design.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Landscape/food-system monitoring with EO and geospatial analytics is a natural knowledge-platform role.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Multifunctional landscapes and food systems are core Alliance themes; GEF-9 is in its first programming year.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Depends on agency partnership; strong fit for MRV/EO components.
opportunities.recommendation: Position the Alliance early with FAO (Food Systems IP) and CI/WWF/IUCN for GEF-9 child projects in LAC, offering EO-based landscape monitoring and crop-climate analytics.
opportunities.potential_partners: FAO, IFAD, UNDP, CI, WWF-US, IUCN, CAF, IDB; CIFOR-ICRAF.
opportunities.next_action: Identify GEF-9 Food Systems/Forest Biomes IP lead agencies and LAC countries; request meetings with agency GEF coordinators.
